item.title: Launch of the CEN Workshop 'European Food Fraud Community of Practice (EFF-CoP)'
item.description: A new CEN Workshop is being established to develop recommendations for self-assessment in relation to food fraud. The Workshop stems from work being done in EFF-CoP – a European project designed to combat food fraud and improve supply chain transparency across Europe. Food fraud is a serious problem in the agri-food business. Due to its highly integrated single market, European companies are especially susceptible, with effects being felt both in terms of economics and public health. Instances of food fraud include substitution, dilution, mislabelling, counterfeiting, and concealment – all of which demonstrate intentional deception for economic gain. item.title: Keeping Drones Within Safe Boundaries: Three European Standards for Safer Flights
item.description: As unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), commonly known as drones, become more common in European skies, a question arises: how can we ensure that these aircraft remain within authorized areas and can be brought safely to the ground when something goes wrong? This matters especially near airports, restricted zones and densely populated areas, where an unexpected flight path may endanger people. Three European Standards—EN 4709-003:2026, EN 4709-005:2026 and EN 4709-006:2026—address this challenge. Developed by CEN/TC 471 ‘Unmanned Aircraft Systems’, they offer complementary requirements and verification methods, from anticipating airspace infringement to containing an aircraft and, as a last resort, terminating its flight. item.title: Not your standard magazine
item.description: A0 for architectural plans, C1 for oversized certificates and DL (DIN long) for the longest sentence in German literature: there are standards behind the formats we use every day. To show that standards can also inspire creativity, DIN created a magazine with a twist: 45 pages in 45 different paper sizes. Each page features a unique interpretation of its paper size, brought to life by artists, designers and other creative minds. The unusual concept has also caught the attention of the creative industry, winning several awards, including a Bronze Lion at the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity. Watch the video to discover the magazine in all its formats. TAGS: Newsletter On the spot Members

item.title: CEN and CENELEC Activities
item.description: We are pleased to inform you about the upcoming CEN and CENELEC activities in 2026. 3 November – RISERS Conference – How can Europe drive cross-sectoral resource efficiency? Upscaling industrial symbiosis through standardization The conference will bring together representatives of industry, research, policymaking and standardization to discuss how Europe can accelerate the implementation of industrial symbiosis across sectors. The event will present the key results of the RISERS project, including the Industrial Symbiosis Standardization Roadmap, and explore the role of standards in bridging innovation and market deployment, supporting European policy objectives and reducing barriers to industrial collaboration. item.title: World Standards Day 2026: Powering a Clean Energy Future for Consumers
item.description: On 14 October, ANEC joined the global celebration of World Standards Day 2026, under the theme “Shared vision for a better world: Spotlight on SDG 7 – Affordable and Clean Energy”. Through its campaign “How can standards ensure clean energy powers a sustainable and inclusive future for consumers?”, ANEC highlighted the role of standards in ensuring an affordable, clean and inclusive energy transition. From 9 to 14 October, ANEC's social media campaign addressed Ecodesign and Energy Labelling, energy-efficient buildings, cybersecurity, the Digital Product Passport and sustainable communities, while emphasizing consumer participation in standardization. item.title: Final stretch before the publication of harmonized standards in support of the AI Act
item.description: The ETUC participated in the 15th CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 Artificial Intelligence Plenary and Working Group meetings, held from 6 to 9 October in Winterthur, Switzerland. Following amendments adopted under the Digital Omnibus on AI in June 2026, the entry into force of obligations for high-risk AI systems was postponed due essentially to the unavailability of the harmonized standards necessary for their implementation. Consequently, the European Commission’s standardization request has been revised to align with the new timelines, setting the deadline for supporting harmonized standards for February 2027. item.title: Croatian Standards Institute celebrates World Standards Day and marks the 18th Electrical Engineering Days
item.description: The Croatian Standards Institute (HZN) marked World Standards Day on 14 October by holding the sixth session of its Technical Council, bringing together HZN members, Governing Board representatives and staff. Participants included Mr Goran Romek, State Secretary at the Ministry of Economy and President of HZN’s Governing Board. HZN Director General Ana Marija Boljanović presented the Institute’s half-year report, highlighting key achievements and activities in European and international standardization, including digitalization, artificial intelligence and developments in the European Standardization System. item.title: A Week of Global Engagement and Collaboration for IFAN in Paris
item.description: Reflecting on a high-impact week in Paris, the active presence of the International Federation of Standards Users (IFAN) at both global and national levels reaffirmed the organization's continued commitment to advancing international cooperation and standardization excellence. Kicking Off at the ISO Annual Meeting IFAN began the week participating in the ISO Annual Meeting in Paris. Throughout the opening days, delegates engaged in dynamic discussions, panels, and presentations focusing on the hottest topics and emerging trends shaping the future of global standardization. These sessions provided a vital platform to align international cooperation, address industry challenges, and share best practices across sectors.
